record: Original cosponsor of the FRONTIER Act (introduced by Rep. Jay Obernolte): a tiered federal framework for the most advanced AI models with model cards, risk-management frameworks, independent audits, incident reporting and catastrophic-risk assessments.
Franklin House press release, 2026-07-23; Ripon Advance, 2026-07-27
grade_reason: Franklin has spoken about AI in 2026, mainly as an original cosponsor of the FRONTIER Act, but in his own words he does not acknowledge catastrophic risk; the catastrophic-risk language in the release is Obernolte's.
notes: All 6 required web searches ran this time, plus 1 extra search on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors (7 in total). None found a Franklin statement on superintelligence, extinction, a pause or slowdown, a China agreement or AI safety. I re-opened the FRONTIER Act release (2026-07-23) and confirmed that the quoted sentence is inside Franklin's own quotation and that 'catastrophic risk' appears only in Obernolte's quotation ('protect Americans from catastrophic risk'); Franklin's quotation does not mention safety, risk or dangers. The page-fetch tool would not return the full text verbatim, so a reviewer should still check the exact wording at the source. Caution: one search-engine summary wrongly attributed the 'protect Americans from catastrophic risk' line to Franklin; the release itself attributes it to Obernolte. The release says Franklin joined as an original cosponsor of Obernolte's bill (Ripon Advance frames it as Obernolte and Franklin offering the bill). A reviewer may consider whether cosponsoring a bill with catastrophic-risk assessments merits C under the bill_or_action flag; I kept D because his own words do not mention catastrophic risk. Other AI activity found, all D or before the 2025 cutoff: he supported the Great American AI Act discussion draft (Obernolte and Trahan; Ripon Advance reports him saying it is meant to gather stakeholder feedback, paraphrase not used); the release says he backed more FY27 funding for the Center for AI Standards and Innovation; he introduced the TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act on AI for weather forecasting; he and Rep. McCormick wrote to Commerce Secretary Lutnick about an AI export rule; he served on the 2024 House AI Task Force. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, Casar, 24 September 2026): no source found showing Franklin as a cosponsor; the reported cosponsors are Democrats.
